label: copy-phase input r
explanation: Fires whenever the token r is fed back as input during the copy phase (t > L), i.e. at the step right after the model outputs an r. On dev, it is active on 99.7% of such steps with zero false positives. Activation is near-constant at about 0.8-1.0 of max. In the quartile examples, the lowest values (about 0.68-0.72) came from r copied at the first copy position (r as first original token), while repeated r runs and later positions tended to be highest; this was read off examples and not measured systematically. It does not fire on r in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other copy-phase token; it is insensitive to out_tok, L and next_out. The few misses are tiny activations (<0.05 of max) on other tokens and carry ~0% of mass.

issues: I confirmed the test scores: precision 1.000, recall 0.996, F1 0.998, mass recall 0.99992, correlation 0.997. There were 0 false positives on test.

Misses on test number 337 and hold 0.0% of the activation mass. They are all tiny activations (0.01 to 0.03 of max). About 138 dev cases are an original-phase r at the last original positions (orig_idx 7 to 8, so L=8 or 9). The rest are copy-phase tokens just before a copied r. This is a weak, systematic pre-activation, but it is negligible, so 'does not fire on original-phase r' is true in practice.

The phase is what makes the feature specific. The predicate in_tok==r without the phase term gets precision 0.459 and F1 0.629, so the feature is not a plain 'r' detector. The label correctly says copy-phase.
The magnitude claim (lowest values at the first copy position) is explicitly unmeasured. It is consistent with the examples (0.69 for r at recall_idx 1) but was not verified.
